response: No, current practices often fall short of meeting the guidelines for preparing patients at high risk of falls for discharge home after rehabilitation. Many patients are not adequately assessed for fall risk, and discharge plans may not include sufficient strategies to mitigate fall risks in the home environment. Additionally, patients and their caregivers may not receive adequate education on fall prevention, and follow-up care to monitor and address ongoing fall risks may be lacking. As a result, patients at high risk of falls may be discharged without the necessary support and resources to ensure their safety at home.
